healthcareSystem: Public healthcare is free but severely under-resourced. Private clinics and mission hospitals provide better care. Lilongwe and Blantyre have the best facilities. Rural areas have very limited healthcare.
qualityNotes: Known as 'The Warm Heart of Africa' — people are friendly and helpful. Private hospitals in Lilongwe and Blantyre are adequate for basic care. English is widely spoken in medical settings. Serious conditions require evacuation to South Africa.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in cities open 8am-5pm weekdays, 8am-12pm Saturday. Very limited access in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Lilongwe and Blantyre stock basic medications. Counterfeit drugs are a concern — buy from reputable pharmacies. English is spoken. Bring essential medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is loose. Many medications available without prescription. Quality of medications can be inconsistent. English documentation accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep medications in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. Keep medications in original packaging. English documentation is accepted. Bring extra supplies as local availability is unreliable.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential. Evacuation to Johannesburg or Nairobi may be needed for serious conditions. Ensure coverage for adventure activities around Lake Malawi.

recommended: Yellow Fever (if arriving from endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Malaria is present throughout the country — antimalarial prophylaxis is essential. Bilharzia (schistosomiasis) risk in Lake Malawi.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink. Use bottled or purified water everywhere, including in hotels. Avoid ice unless from a reliable source. Lake Malawi water should not be consumed.
foodSafetyTips: Eat thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruits from street vendors. Nsima (cornmeal staple) served with cooked relish is generally safe at restaurants. Be cautious with lake fish — ensure it is well cooked.
medicalTourismNote: Malawi is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialist care travel to Johannesburg, Nairobi, or Dar es Salaam.
metaDescription: Health guide for Malawi: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Kamuzu Central Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public referral hospital in the capital. English-speaking staff. Can be overcrowded.

hospitals.name: Mwaiwathu Private Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best private hospital in Malawi. Good standard of care. Preferred by expats and tourists.

hospitals.name: Partners in Hope Medical Centre
hospitals.notes: Well-equipped medical center. Good reputation for quality care.

hospitals.name: Nkhoma Mission Hospital
hospitals.notes: Mission hospital with decent standards. Useful for travelers between Lilongwe and the lake.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

pharmacyPhrases.transliteration: ndee-lee ndee ah-LER-jee (Chichewa; English loanword used)

dentalCare.availability: Limited dental care in Lilongwe and Blantyre. Very few dentists in the country.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics offer basic care. Equipment may be outdated. English-speaking dentists available.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Mwaiwathu Private Hospital in Blantyre has dental services. In Lilongwe, ask at private clinics.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. A few counselors available through NGOs in Lilongwe.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited. Bring all psychiatric medications from home with ample supply.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited. Most buildings lack ramps and wheelchair access. Roads are rough.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals have basic wheelchair access. Smaller clinics do not.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Hire private vehicles. Many roads are unpaved.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility impairments will face significant challenges. Lake Malawi lodges vary — confirm accessibility before booking. Bring any needed mobility equipment.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at major hospitals in Lilongwe and Blantyre.
covidStatus.notes: Malaria, bilharzia from Lake Malawi, and waterborne diseases are more significant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals require upfront cash payment (Malawian Kwacha or USD). Keep all receipts. English documentation provided. Public hospitals are free but under-resourced.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public healthcare is free but very basic. Local currency is Malawian Kwacha (MWK).

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential. Local healthcare cannot handle serious emergencies. Johannesburg is the primary evacuation destination with world-class hospitals.

drugNameMap.note: Panadol is the most common brand. Generic paracetamol widely available.

Available at pharmacies in Lilongwe and Blantyre. Bring your own for rural travel.
